text:
perf-ci-bot: perf/regression detected on staging: token/sec -27% vs baseline after deploy (refs/heads/main @ 0f9a3c2) :rotating_light:

sana: seeing the alert, perf dashboard shows continuous-batcher output drop. digging in now.

andrew: is this the rollout from earlier today? deploy-bot shows merge of PR #4321 (adaptive-coalesce heuristics).

deploy-bot: deploy completed — build 2026-03-18-09:12 UTC, rolled to staging.

jia: quick profiling snapshot (top-level):
```
continuous_batch_wait_ms: +41
kernel_memcpy_ms: +9
kernel_select: fallback->gemm increased 48%
kv_cache_hitrate: -15%
```

mike: kv hit drop and memcpy spike smells like kernel path mismatch for short-seq requests. the new heuristic might be preferring a kernel that does extra device->host copies for packing.

sana: running `perf bisect` now to narrow commits between 0e7b9a (good) and 0f9a3c2 (bad). will post steps.

andrew: if it's the kernel policy, can we force the old kernel as a quick canary? i.e. env `REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF=legacy_gemm` for staging pool.

jia: +1 for pinning as a mitigation while we bisect. also plan to run a microbench to confirm memcpy time.

sana: bisect plan:
```
git checkout 0f9a3c2
git bisect start
git bisect bad
git bisect good 0e7b9a
# run microbench harness: tools/ctb_bench --seq-dist=short --warmup=2000 --tokens=100k
# record token/sec
```

perf-ci-bot: attached job 6721 with autoprofiler output (link: https://perf.redwood/6721)

mike: I ran the microbench locally against a couple commits. early result: commit 0f3d2a9 (PR #4318) increases memcpy by ~8ms due to a changed packing path in kernel selector.

andrew: that PR touched the `select_kernel_for_batch` heuristic to prefer presumed-fused kernels when batch_count>1. maybe the short sequences end up with a different path.

sana: thanks — can someone try: 1) pin kernel to `legacy_gemm` on staging 2) revert PR #4318 in a canary 3) run microbench?

jia: pinning `legacy_gemm` on a single canary node now (staging/slot-3). will run the same harness and report.

[some minutes pass]

jia: harness after pin: token/sec back within 3% of baseline, memcpy ms back down. kv hit still slightly low but within noise.

mike: confirms: kernel pin restores throughput. looks like the selector change caused fallback memcopies for small sequences.

andrew: short-term action: hold rollout and patch PR #4318 to refine condition (require seq_len_mean>32 AND batch_size>4 before choosing fused kernel).

sana: opened PR #4330 to tighten the heuristic and added a regression test in `tests/perf/ctb_kernel_select_test.py`. linking: https://git.redwood/4330

perf-ci-bot: CI run triggered for PR #4330 — perf smoke scheduled.

mike: long-term: we should add an integration microbench to CI that simulates short-seq heavy traffic so selector regressions are caught earlier. filing a follow-up issue.

andrew: also add a telemetry counter for kernel route frequencies and per-kernel memcpy_time so operator console can alert when memcpy increases unexpectedly.

sana: plan for release: revert/hold main rollout, merge #4330 once CI perf passes, then do canary with pinned canary->unpin->incremental rollout.

jia: agreed. holding the main rollout now and notifying infra to keep capacity. :thumbsup:

andrew: thanks team — great catch from perf-ci. 

sana: next steps captured in thread. I'll follow up with a postmortem once we've merged and validated the patch. :memo:
